title: Bounded-staleness KV reclamation with prefix affinity and lease-protected compaction
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem statement:
Continuous batching and prefix-aware KV caching increase GPU memory efficiency but create tricky correctness windows during eviction/compaction. Ongoing issues we want to avoid: (1) in-flight batches referencing KV entries that are concurrently reclaimed, (2) prefix-grouped reclamation creating unexpected memory pressure spikes, and (3) nondeterministic behavior between LRU and TTL heuristics when prefixes have divergent access patterns.

Goals:
- Define a reclamation protocol that guarantees safe reclamation without stalling continuous batching pipeline.
- Keep tail-latency and throughput targets for hosted tier unchanged (SLOs).
- Maintain reproducible correctness invariants so we can assert no stale KV references remain in completed generations.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a lease-protected, two-phase reclamation flow with prefix affinity grouping and bounded-staleness semantics. High-level components:
1) Lease acquisition: when a batch touches a prefix scope, it pins leases on prefix bucket metadata (cheap atomic increment on CPU control plane). Leases are short-lived (configurable, default 250ms) and renewed automatically if the batch pipeline expects more tokens.
2) Soft reclamation pass: LRU/TTL heuristics select candidates per prefix-bucket. Selected entries enter a 'quarantine' state (soft-reclaimed) marked by a version stamp and soft-expiry timestamp. Quarantined entries remain readable but can be excluded from new cache-warm decisions.
3) Hard reclaim only after lease expiry and a grace window: once no active leases exist for the prefix and the grace window (bounded-staleness, default 2s) expired, a compaction op reclaims GPU memory for entries whose version equals the final quarantined stamp. Compaction uses page-aligned frees and invokes a lightweight GC callback that ensures no existing GPU kernel holds a stale pointer (see correctness section).
4) Prefix-affinity scheduler: eviction decisions are scored by (expected reuse, prefix activity, size, contiguity in GPU memory). We bias reclamation away from hot prefixes and prefer contiguous regions to reduce fragmentation and kernel bookkeeping costs.

Why this is different from naive LRU/TTL:
- LRU alone can evict just-before-use under continuous batching; TTL alone can keep cold prefixes for too long. Combining soft-quarantine with short leases guarantees that in-flight batches see a consistent view while still allowing aggressive reclamation when safe.
- Prefix affinity preserves temporal locality and reduces fragmentation by preferring contiguous regions for compaction.

Invariants and correctness guarantees (must be testable):
INV-1 (no dangling GPU pointers): After compaction completes, no kernel executing on any GPU may reference memory returned to the allocator. We ensure this by versioned handles + GPU kernel fence + post-fence reclamation.
INV-2 (bounded staleness): Any KV read may return an entry that was soft-quarantined at most G seconds ago (G = grace window). This bounds how stale prefix data can be observed by downstream generation paths.
INV-3 (lease soundness): If a batch held any lease touching a prefix at time T, then entries in that prefix will not be hard-reclaimed until T + lease_ttl + grace_window.
INV-4 (atomic pointer swap): When a hot entry is updated in-place (hot rewrite), consumers either see the old version or the new version, but never a partially-updated inside a generation. Achieved by double-buffer writes with version stamps.

Implementation notes:
- Control-plane metadata: prefix-buckets maintain counters for leases, quarantined counts, and a monotonic version stamp. Keep this metadata off-GPU in a compact sharded map (per-GPU and per-CPU control copy).
- GPU-side allocation: maintain slab allocator with prefix-aware arenas. Each allocation carries a 64-bit version tag stored in a host-visible header.
- Lease lifecycle: batches call acquire_lease(prefix_id) at pipeline boundary and release_lease(prefix_id) after their final KV access. SDKs/serving runtime will automatically manage leases for the common inference paths.
- Quarantine marking: mark entries by updating version_tag -> (version | QUARANTINE_FLAG) using atomic store on host metadata; no immediate device-side free.
- Compaction: compaction thread obtains a per-GPU compaction lock, waits for GPU fence that corresponds to the last kernel touching the region, verifies version == quarantined stamp, then frees region atomically via allocator API.
- Fallback: if compaction would cause temporary OOM because it's too aggressive, fallback to conservative LRU-only pass and emit a diagnostic metric and alert.

Decisions and trade-offs:
- Lease TTL vs throughput: longer leases are safer but increase memory pressure. We pick conservative defaults (250ms) with dynamic tuning by the optimizer based on observed prefix activity.
- Grace window sizing: 2s default strikes balance between tail-safety for streaming pipelines and memory reclamation pace. Can be reduced for low-latency, high-throughput customers.
- Metadata locality: keeping metadata off-GPU costs an extra hop but simplifies correctness reasoning and reduces kernel ABI complexity.
- Fragmentation vs contiguity: preferring contiguous frees during compaction can delay reclamation for scattered cold objects. We mitigate by opportunistic small frees when contiguous thresholds aren't reached.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests that exercise INV-1 through INV-4 deterministically.
- Property-based fuzz harness proving no dangling pointer reads under randomized batch interleavings (see test plan).
- Performance benchmark: end-to-end gen throughput within 3% of baseline and 99th percentile latency regression <= 5% on our canary workload.
- Canaries: rollout to 10% of inference traffic in staging, 5% of production for non-critical customers, monitor for metric regressions for 48h before wider rollout.

acceptance_criteria:
- Deterministic unit tests proving no dangling GPU pointer after compaction.
- Fuzz harness (10k randomized runs) with zero correctness failures.
- Performance: <=3% throughput drop; <=5% 99th latency regression on canary workload.
- No OOM incidents in 48h canary on production pass.
- Metrics: prefix-miss-rate, quarantine-duration-p95, compaction-duration-p95, gpu-free-bytes-trend
implementation_notes: See description for allocator and metadata design. Additional implementation tasks below. Key APIs to add: acquire_lease(prefix_id) -> lease_token, renew_lease(token), release_lease(token), mark_quarantine(handle, version), compact_prefix(prefix_id, target_bytes). Use GPU fences: streamFenceForHandle(handle) -> host-fence-id. Allocator must support free_if_version(handle, version_stamp).
tasks: Add lease API to runtime control plane and SDKs
Implement prefix-bucket metadata sharding and counters
Modify slab allocator to include per-allocation version tags
Quarantine marking and soft eviction path implementation
Compaction thread with GPU fence coordination
Property-based fuzz tests and deterministic concurrency harness
End-to-end perf benchmark and dashboard integration
Canary rollout automation and alerting rules
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for allocator free_if_version semantics.
2) Deterministic concurrency replay harness reproducing sequences of lease acquire/release + quarantines.
3) Property-based fuzzing with 10k seeds across different lease_ttl and grace_window combos.
4) Stress tests with continuous batching enabling and disabling prefix affinity to validate fragmentation behavior.
5) Simulated OOM injection tests to validate fallback path and alerting.
6) Integration canary: run with 10% staging traffic for 24h, then 5% prod for 48h.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: merge feature flags off by default; run internal QA with debug metrics.
Phase 2: enable staging canary (10% of staging traffic) for 24h; verify metrics.
Phase 3: enable prod canary for non-critical customers at 5% traffic for 48h; escalate on any OOM/correctness/latency regression.
Phase 4: gradual ramp with automated rollback on regression thresholds.
notes: Recent experiments: preliminary staging runs show quarantine-duration-p95 ~= 1.6s and no observed dangling pointer violations in 100 deterministic runs. Fragmentation reduced by ~12% vs naive per-object frees when compaction uses prefix-contiguity. Open question: autoscaling knob for lease TTL based on observed prefix churn. Recommend a follow-up spike to prototype the tuner (ENG-42001).
